name: Crossref REST API
purpose: Primary keyless discovery + metadata service: search, works/<doi> lookup, is-referenced-by-count, journal/container queries, DOI content-negotiation to BibTeX/CSL.
keys_required: no (an email in the User-Agent, which polite_get.py already sends, moves you to Crossref's faster 'polite' pool; no account)
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=pdf+repair&rows=1' -> HTTP 200, total-results=457305; works/<doi>, journals/<issn>/works and content-negotiation to application/x-bibtex all returned HTTP 200 on 2026-09-27 (see OBS-0600 and probe/crossref*.json, probe/das2018.bib)
rationale: Already the KB's main discovery+metadata backbone (used throughout research/sources/registry.jsonl). OBS-0600 shows it is the more complete of the two free forward-citation sources (0/10 zero-count sources vs OpenCitations' 5/10). Also answers sub-task 7: DOI to BibTeX/CSL via /works/<doi>/transform/<mime> works keyless, tested live. Serves W1/W2 discovery and P4 full review broadly; feeds forward-citation checks for any gap that depends on knowing whether a source has since been superseded or corroborated.

name: OpenCitations (Index API v2 / COCI)
purpose: Free, keyless forward-citation lookup (citations/references graph) to cross-check Crossref's is-referenced-by-count.
keys_required: no (an optional free access token raises the rate limit; not required for the volumes we need)
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://opencitations.net/index/api/v2/citations/doi:10.1109/das.2018.64' -> HTTP 200, body [] (0 citers), 2026-09-27; run again for 10 sources in OBS-0600
rationale: OBS-0600: agrees closely with Crossref for ACM/Elsevier/PoPETs venues, but under-covers IEEE and 2024+ works (misses 2 citations Crossref already has for SRC-0112, a 2024 IEEE TIFS paper), confirming the needs-table's DAS-2018/CPR observation and extending it. Use as a secondary cross-check, not the primary source: Crossref (TOOL-300) is more complete. Serves W1/W2 forward-citation coverage; backs OBS-0600.

name: arXiv API (export.arxiv.org)
purpose: Keyless discovery and full-text access for preprints in CS/physics-adjacent subfields (compression, some forensics/ML crossover).
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2101.00001' -> HTTP 406 twice (60s backoff each), 2026-09-27, despite this being a documented known-good id lookup; not retried further per the no-retry-loop rule
rationale: Contradicts the needs-table's 'arXiv id lookups work' note as tested today; most likely transient shared-IP contention from other Stage-2 agents hitting export.arxiv.org concurrently (MIN_GAP=3s is per-process, not per-container-wide across agents), not a permanent block. Still needed for GROBID/Nougat benchmark papers (arXiv 2303.09957, 2410.09871) which the chair should re-fetch via WebFetch/browser if the API stays flaky. Re-test before relying on it in P4.

name: DBLP
purpose: CS bibliography search, useful for venue/author disambiguation (DFRWS, ICDAR, JCDL proceedings listings).
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://dblp.org/search?q=pdf+repair' -> HTTP 200 but body is a within.website anti-bot challenge page ('Making sure you're not a bot!'), 2026-09-27
rationale: Confirms the needs-table's 'DBLP serves an anti-bot page' finding with a fresh, dated test. DBLP's static XML dump (dblp.org/xml/) may be usable offline instead, but that is a multi-hundred-MB download, over what one literature-pipeline check should spend; not attempted here. Hold for live API use; Assess the static-dump route separately if a future agent needs full DBLP coverage.

name: OpenAlex API
purpose: Large open discovery index (works, concepts, citation graph) with broad multidisciplinary + IEEE/ACM coverage; would help close the discovery gap the needs-table flags.
cost: free (a free account and a mailto/API key raise the rate limit)
keys_required: no key for baseline use, but keyless requests were throttled today; a free account removes the throttle
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.openalex.org/works?search=pdf+repair&per-page=1' -> HTTP 429 twice (60s backoff each), 2026-09-27; not retried further
rationale: Confirms the needs-table's 'OpenAlex returns 429 without keys' state with a fresh test. OpenAlex's polite-pool/mailto and free-API-key mechanism is well documented (docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api, which now redirects to help.openalex.org) but this agent could not pull today's exact numeric quota through WebFetch's page summarizer on 2026-09-27, so the specific rate-limit figures below are not independently reconfirmed this session and should be treated as Assess-level until a future agent re-checks them directly. Recommended for the API-account list (see report.md): likely the single highest-value free key for W1, since OpenAlex indexes IEEE/ACM/Elsevier venues that OpenCitations under-covers (OBS-0600).

name: Semantic Scholar Graph API
purpose: Discovery + citation graph + occasional full-text/TLDR summaries; strong CS/ML coverage.
cost: free (higher, steadier throughput with a free API key)
keys_required: no key for baseline use, but keyless requests were throttled today
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=pdf+repair&limit=1' -> HTTP 429 twice (60s backoff each), 2026-09-27; not retried further
rationale: Confirms the needs-table's 'Semantic Scholar returns 429 without keys' state with a fresh test. semanticscholar.org/product/api documents a free API-key request form ('you will receive your private API key via email'); this agent could not extract today's exact numeric rate-limit figures via WebFetch's summarizer (one fetch attempt returned an implausible '1000 requests per second' figure that looks like a misread and is not trusted), so treat any specific quota number as unverified until a future agent confirms it directly against the live docs. Recommended for the API-account list alongside OpenAlex.

name: CORE API
purpose: Large open-access aggregator (repositories + journals); keyless search with a real, usable free tier.
cost: free (a free registration raises the rate limit further, not required for baseline use)
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.core.ac.uk/v3/search/works?q=pdf+repair&limit=1' -> HTTP 200, totalHits=4978068, 2026-09-27 (probe/core.json); CORE's own terms page confirms keyless access at 'one batch request or five single requests per 10 seconds' with no registration required
rationale: The single best surprise of the discovery sweep: works keyless from this container with real, large result sets, contradicting a plausible assumption that CORE needs a key. Directly answers the needs-table's 'which free keyed services would unblock discovery' question by showing CORE needs none. Also doubles as a full-text-access path (aggregates repository copies). Serves W1/W2 discovery and sub-task 3 (full-text access).

name: Europe PMC REST API
purpose: Biomedical-leaning discovery/full-text service (the PubMed MCP connected to this environment is also biomedical); checked for edge-case coverage of forensics/OCR papers that stray into life-sciences venues.
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py '.../search?query=pdf+repair&format=json' -> HTTP 200, hitCount=879598, 2026-09-27 (probe/europepmc.json)
rationale: Works keyless with a huge index, but its subject-matter centre of gravity (biomedical/life-sciences) barely overlaps PDFPundit's fields (forensics, LangSec, compression, fonts/OCR, IEEE/ACM venues); the same gap the already-connected PubMed MCP has. Keep as a low-priority fallback for the rare life-sciences-adjacent OCR/accessibility paper, not a primary discovery route.

name: BASE (Bielefeld Academic Search Engine)
purpose: Repository-aggregating discovery/full-text search named explicitly in the brief's sub-task 1 list.
keys_required: normally no for basic search, but see verdict
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://www.base-search.net/Search/Results?func=PHP...&format=json' -> HTTP 200 but body is '<error>Access denied for IP address 160.79.106.128 and user agent PDFPundit-research/0.1 (...)</error>', 2026-09-27 (probe/base.xml)
rationale: Concrete, quotable denial: BASE is blocking this container's shared IP and/or its declared User-Agent outright, not merely rate-limiting. Per the no-retry/no-workaround rule this was not retried with a different UA or via WebFetch. Hold until a future agent can test from a different egress path; do not spend more of the discovery budget on BASE.

name: Lens.org / Dimensions (commercial scholarly search)
purpose: Named in the brief's sub-task 1 list as additional discovery services to evaluate; both offer patent + scholarly search with richer analytics than the free APIs above.
cost: freemium (Lens.org: free tier with a registered account and daily query caps; Dimensions: mostly institutional/paid, with a limited free web UI)
keys_required: yes, a free account for Lens.org's API; Dimensions' API is normally institutional-licence-gated
verification_evidence: Not tested: both require account signup to use programmatically, and 'sign up for accounts' is on this agent's never-do list, so no live call was attempted
rationale: provenance.method is memory for the account/quota details above (general knowledge of both products, not re-derived from a fresh fetch this session); capped at Assess accordingly, and further capped by the account-signup block. Only worth an account if OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/CORE prove insufficient in P4 — those three already cover the bulk of our venues keyless or with a free key.

name: Unpaywall API
purpose: Keyless full-text/OA-location lookup by DOI; the brief names it explicitly and mandates the research@pdfpundit.invalid contact email over any real address.
keys_required: an email query parameter (not an account); this agent used research@pdfpundit.invalid per the brief
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1109/das.2018.64?email=research@pdfpundit.invalid' -> HTTP 200, {"is_oa":false,"oa_status":"closed",...}, 2026-09-27 (probe/unpaywall.json)
rationale: Confirms the needs-table's 'Unpaywall works keyless' state with a fresh, dated, first-hand test (previously only asserted, not independently re-verified this session). Correctly reports closed access for a known-closed IEEE paper, giving confidence in its accuracy. Directly serves sub-task 3 (full-text access) alongside CORE and direct PDF fetch.

name: Community MCP paper-search servers (Crossref/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/arXiv/DBLP wrappers)
purpose: Evaluate whether any unofficial MCP server would meaningfully add discovery capability beyond this agent's direct polite_get.py access to the same free APIs.
cost: free (varies by server; typically MIT-licensed community projects)
keys_required: no more than the underlying API already requires
verification_evidence: Not installed or run; assessed from Parallel Search results only (query text reconstructed post-compaction, see SRCH-0613)
rationale: Multiple community MCP servers exist that wrap Crossref/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/arXiv/DBLP search, none official or particularly authoritative; the already-connected PubMed MCP is the only first-party one available here and it is biomedical-only. None of the surveyed community servers offer a discovery capability this agent doesn't already have directly through polite_get.py against the same free APIs, so adding one would mean extra install/maintenance surface for no coverage gain. Revisit only if a future agent needs a scholarly-search MCP wired into a non-Claude-Code client.

name: Elicit
purpose: Hosted AI literature-review assistant (extraction tables, systematic-review support); named explicitly in the brief's sub-task 1.
cost: freemium (free tier with monthly credit limits; paid tiers for higher volume)
verification_evidence: Not tested: requires account signup, which is on this agent's never-do list. Facts below come from the Parallel Search results (SRCH-0614); exact figures not independently re-confirmed this session.
rationale: Per the charter, hosted AI literature tools are research-only and capped at Assess regardless of capability, and this agent could not create an account to verify anything hands-on. Elicit's extraction-table workflow is conceptually close to what sub-task 5 wants (pre-filtering candidate limitation/future-work quotes), but as a closed hosted product it cannot itself produce kb_validate.py-checkable verified quotes; at best it could suggest candidates for an agent to then verify against the real PDF. Not worth an account yet given GROBID/Nougat + a citation-context classifier (TOOL-324) can approximate the same pre-filtering keylessly.

name: Consensus
purpose: Hosted AI search engine over papers, answers yes/no research questions with citations.
verification_evidence: Not tested: requires account signup. Facts from general knowledge, not re-confirmed this session.
rationale: Same charter cap and account block as Elicit. Consensus's yes/no synthesis format is a poor fit for PDFPundit's kind of evidence (verified quotes at a page, not an AI-synthesized answer), so even with an account it would mostly serve as a discovery lead generator, redundant with OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/CORE.

name: scite.ai
purpose: Citation-context classification service (supporting/contrasting/mentioning citations) sold as a hosted product; directly relevant to sub-task 5's citation-context-tool question.
cost: freemium (limited free lookups; subscription for full access)
keys_required: yes, an account for full API access
verification_evidence: Not tested: requires account signup for API-level access. Facts from general knowledge/Parallel Search leads, not re-confirmed this session.
rationale: Conceptually the closest hosted match to sub-task 5 (citation-context classification), but paywalled at the API level and capped at Assess by the charter regardless. TOOL-324 (the open, fine-tunable RoBERTa citance classifier from ACL 2022.sdp-1.6) gives most of the same capability without an account, license fee, or vendor lock-in, and is the preferred route for P4/P5.

name: Connected Papers
purpose: Visual citation-graph explorer for literature mapping; named in the brief's sub-task 1.
cost: freemium (a handful of free graphs, then a paid plan)
keys_required: an account for more than a few free graphs
verification_evidence: Not tested: requires account for sustained use. Facts from general knowledge, not re-confirmed this session.
rationale: Useful as a human-in-the-loop discovery aid (spotting clusters an agent's keyword search missed) but has no API and produces no machine-checkable evidence, so it cannot feed kb_validate.py directly. Capped at Assess by the charter and by the account limit.

name: ResearchRabbit
purpose: Free hosted citation-network / recommendation tool for literature discovery; named in the brief's sub-task 1.
verification_evidence: Not tested: requires account signup. Facts from general knowledge, not re-confirmed this session.
rationale: Same shape as Connected Papers: a useful human discovery aid with no API and no machine-checkable output, blocked from hands-on testing by the account-signup rule and capped at Assess by the charter.

name: GROBID (CRF-only Docker image)
purpose: Reference/metadata/section extraction from academic PDFs via a CRF pipeline (no deep-learning models needed for the CRF-only image), avoiding a multi-GB full image.
verification_evidence: Image size confirmed via Docker Hub v2 API: GET https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/grobid/grobid/tags -> grobid/grobid:0.9.1-crf full_size=509986678 bytes (~486 MiB), 2026-09-27 (probe/dockerhub_grobid.json). Hands-on run not attempted: starting the Docker daemon (`nohup dockerd &`) was denied by the sandbox's auto-mode classifier ('[Unauthorized Persistence]'); per the coordinator's mid-task update this was not retried or worked around.
rationale: At ~486 MiB the CRF-only image comfortably fits the 1.5 GB/tool budget (full image is ~14 GB, out of the question). arXiv 2303.09957 (found via SRCH-0617) reports GROBID best-in-class for academic-PDF metadata/reference extraction among 10 compared tools, which is strong published support for making it the primary reference-list extractor once a future agent (with Docker access) can actually run it. Recommend a P4 hands-on trial the moment a Docker daemon is available.
alternatives: pymupdf4llm (TOOL-323, hands-on Adopt for section/heading structure)

name: Docling
purpose: Document-conversion library (PDF/DOCX/etc. to structured Markdown/JSON) with layout and table models, from IBM/LF AI.
verification_evidence: Version from PyPI JSON (pypi.org/pypi/docling/json, probe/pypi_docling.json), 2026-09-27. PyPI metadata's own 'license' field is null; confirmed MIT by fetching raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/LICENSE directly, 2026-09-27 (probe/docling_license.txt). Not run: its ML-based layout model would likely need a model download beyond a quick check within this session's remaining time/disk budget.
rationale: Actively developed (v2.130.0), permissively licensed (MIT, resolved from source since PyPI metadata alone was silent), and a plausible GROBID alternative or complement, but not hands-on verified here. Vendor/grey-lit benchmarks surfaced via SRCH-0617 (inferensys.com, ertas.ai, docs.bswen.com) put it competitive with Marker/Nougat on general documents but these are not peer-reviewed and are treated as low-authority context, not evidence.

name: Marker (marker-pdf)
purpose: PDF-to-Markdown converter aimed at documents/books, with layout, table and equation handling.
cost: free (a paid hosted API also exists)
verification_evidence: Version + license from PyPI JSON (pypi.org/pypi/marker-pdf/json, probe/pypi_marker-pdf.json), 2026-09-27.
rationale: Cleanly licensed (Apache-2.0) and a live project, but not hands-on tested here (its OCR/layout backends pull larger model weights than fit comfortably in this check's time budget). Grey-lit benchmarks (SRCH-0617) rate it well on general/book-style PDFs; no peer-reviewed comparison specific to academic papers was found, unlike GROBID/Nougat.

name: MinerU
purpose: PDF-to-structured-content pipeline (layout, OCR, formula, table) popular in the LLM-data-prep community; the brief flags a licence concern by version.
license: Apache-2.0 with an additional commercial-use-threshold clause (current, v4.0.7)
cost: free for research/most commercial use under the threshold
verification_evidence: License history resolved by direct fetch, not memory: raw.githubusercontent.com/opendatalab/MinerU/master/LICENSE.md (current) begins 'MinerU is licensed under Apache License 2.0 and is subject to the additional terms below... Commercial License and Thresholds', fetched 2026-09-27 (probe/mineru_license.md); the git tag mineru-2.5.0-released (matching the brief's '2509' = Sept 2025) instead has raw.githubusercontent.com/opendatalab/MinerU/mineru-2.5.0-released/LICENSE.md as the full GNU AGPLv3 text, fetched 2026-09-27 (probe/mineru_2.5.0_license.md). PyPI metadata's own license field is null for the current release.
rationale: The brief's '2509 is AGPL' warning is confirmed exactly: MinerU v2.5.0 (tagged Sept 2025) is AGPL-3.0, a copyleft licence PDFPundit's clean-room rule would flag for any linked/derivative use; but the current v4.0.7 (and PyPI 'mineru') has since relicensed to Apache-2.0 plus a commercial-MAU/revenue-threshold addendum, which is compatible with research use and most non-trivial commercial use. Any future agent must pin the exact version used and re-check LICENSE.md at that tag, since this project has changed licence at least once.

name: Nougat (nougat-ocr)
purpose: Meta AI's vision-transformer OCR model for converting scientific PDF pages (with equations) to Markdown; the brief flags the model weights as non-commercial.
license: MIT (code, per PyPI classifier); the pretrained model weights are released separately under CC BY-NC 4.0 per the project's own README (not independently re-fetched this session -- treat this specific weight-licence claim as memory until a future agent confirms it against the current README/model card)
cost: free (code); weights are gated to non-commercial use if the README claim above holds
verification_evidence: Code license MIT confirmed from PyPI JSON classifiers (pypi.org/pypi/nougat-ocr/json, probe/pypi_nougat-ocr.json), 2026-09-27. Not run: downloading the model weights (~1.3-3.8 GB depending on model size) risked exceeding a comfortable share of the 1.5 GB/tool budget alongside the pdfplumber/pymupdf4llm run already done this session, so it was skipped rather than rushed.
rationale: arXiv 2410.09871v1 (SRCH-0617) reports Nougat as the strongest of the compared tools specifically for scientific-document text/equation extraction, which is real published support -- but the weight-licence restriction (if confirmed) would make it research-only, and this agent could not fit a hands-on run inside the session's remaining disk budget. A future agent with more headroom should download the smaller 'small' checkpoint, hands-on test it on the same CPR PDF used for OBS-0601, and re-confirm the weight licence from Meta's current model card before any Adopt/Trial upgrade.

name: pdfplumber
purpose: Pure-Python PDF text/table extraction library; a lightweight alternative to pdftotext with programmatic access to character/line positions.
verification_evidence: OBS-0601: pip-installed into a scratch venv (369 MB, deleted after the run) and run on the cached CPR PDF (SRC-0123, sha256 73f1223...): extracted all page text in 4.2s, found the References section (unheaded) and the paper's own limitations sentence intact, but its default extract_text() spliced two unrelated columns together at one checked two-column boundary, an error the pdftotext baseline also makes at the same spot; 2026-09-27
rationale: Runs cleanly and is the lightest-weight option, but the confirmed two-column-merge defect (shared with plain pdftotext) means it needs pdfplumber's layout/column-detection options (not exercised in this quick check) before it could safely feed an automated limitation/future-work extraction step. pymupdf4llm (TOOL-323) avoided this specific defect out of the box in the same test.

name: PyMuPDF4LLM (pymupdf4llm)
purpose: PyMuPDF-based PDF-to-Markdown converter aimed at LLM-ingestion pipelines, with heading-level detection.
license: AGPL-3.0-or-later, OR Artifex's commercial licence (dual-licensed, same as PyMuPDF core)
cost: free under AGPL for AGPL-compatible (e.g. research/internal, non-distributed) use; a commercial licence is needed to ship it inside a closed-source product
verification_evidence: OBS-0601: pip-installed into a scratch venv (369 MB total with pdfplumber, deleted after) and run on the cached CPR PDF: converted to Markdown in 7.9s, correctly leveled every section heading (Introduction..Conclusion), located '### References' as its own heading with individually separated entries, and stayed column-clean at the same two-column boundary where pdfplumber and pdftotext both garbled the text; 2026-09-27
rationale: The strongest hands-on result of this sweep: real heading structure plus a cleaner two-column read than either pdfplumber or the existing pdftotext baseline, directly useful for isolating a paper's Conclusion/Limitations text for sub-task 5. Its AGPL-3.0-or-later licence (the free option of the dual licence) is copyleft: fine for this research pipeline's own internal use (we are not distributing it or linking it into the PDFPundit product, which is the pure-Rust/lopdf-only artifact under the charter's clean-room rule), but flag it clearly so no one later vendors its output-generation code into the shipped tool.

name: Citance/citation-context classification (published methods, e.g. ACL 2022.sdp-1.6) and future-work/limitation sentence extraction
purpose: Published, open-access methods for classifying citation context (supporting/contrasting/background) and for extracting future-work/limitation sentences from paper text, evaluated as a possible pre-filter for candidate quotes.
license: paper: open access (ACL Anthology, CC BY); any released code/model would carry its own separate licence, not checked here
cost: free (paper); compute cost only if a fine-tuned classifier is reproduced
verification_evidence: Found via Parallel Search (SRCH-0617): ACL Anthology 2022.sdp-1.6 reports a fine-tuned RoBERTa classifier for citation-context criticality at 98.84% accuracy; not fetched/cached or run in this session.
rationale: Directly answers sub-task 5's 'citation-context tools' question with a real, open-access, peer-reviewed method rather than a hosted product (contrast TOOL-314 scite.ai, which does the same thing behind a paywall). In principle such a classifier could pre-filter candidate limitation/future-work sentences for other agents, but it cannot replace kb_validate.py's exact-quote/page check: at best it narrows which sentences a human or agent then verifies by hand against the real PDF. Worth caching this paper as a proper SRC/CLM record and, if a future agent has GPU/CPU headroom, reproducing or reusing a small citation-context classifier as a P4/P5 pre-filter -- not attempted here to stay inside this session's time budget.

name: Dedicated reference manager (e.g. Zotero/BetterBibTeX-style tooling) vs plain JSONL
purpose: Assess whether the knowledge base should adopt a dedicated reference-manager layer on top of, or instead of, the existing JSONL registries.
verification_evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py '.../works/10.1109/das.2018.64/transform/application/x-bibtex' -> HTTP 200, valid @inproceedings{...} BibTeX record, 2026-09-27 (probe/das2018.bib); Crossref's content-negotiation also serves CSL-JSON via Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json on the same works/<doi> URL
rationale: Crossref content negotiation already gives DOI to BibTeX/CSL-JSON on demand, keyless, with no extra service to install or maintain; every source in the KB already carries its DOI in registry.jsonl, so any reference-manager format can be regenerated on demand rather than stored and kept in sync. Introducing a separate reference manager (Zotero, JabRef, etc.) would add a second source of truth to reconcile with the JSONL registries for no capability we lack -- Hold on adopting one. If a human collaborator later wants a browsable/exportable citation library, generate it from registry.jsonl + Crossref content negotiation as a one-off script rather than maintaining a live reference-manager library.

name: warcio
purpose: Read/write WARC records (payload + headers) for Common Crawl truncation-pair sampling (GAP-100).
rationale: Not installed/exercised this session: research/experiments/cc_natural_pairs.py and this agent's own extension already implement a minimal hand-rolled WARC-gzip parser (parse_warc()) sufficient for range-read single-record extraction, so warcio was not load-bearing for OBS-0800/OBS-0201. Worth adopting if the sampler grows beyond single-record reads (e.g. iterating whole WARC files).

name: cdx_toolkit + Common Crawl CDX server (index.commoncrawl.org)
purpose: Look up WARC offsets for arbitrary URLs via the CDX index, as an alternative to digitalcorpora's pre-built provenance CSV (GAP-100).
verification_evidence: curl to index.commoncrawl.org: http_code=000 (connection failure); a polite_get.py attempt raised a raw urllib/http.client ConnectionError-style exception. $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status shows a 'ws_closed_mid_exchange' relay failure for index.commoncrawl.org:443 at 2026-09-27T17:50Z (two occurrences), i.e. the tunnel opens then closes after ~6s with almost no bytes exchanged -- an origin/TLS-negotiation problem, not a proxy policy denial like corpora.tika.apache.org's 502. Not retried further per standing instruction.
rationale: cdx_toolkit itself (pip package) is unremarkable and would install fine, but it is useless here while its only server is unreachable from this container. digitalcorpora's pre-built full provenance CSV (used successfully in OBS-0800) is a working substitute for the CC-MAIN-2021-31 corpus specifically.

name: digitalcorpora unsigned-S3 range-fetch technique
purpose: Discover and range-read corpus files/metadata on digitalcorpora's public S3 bucket without an AWS account, for GAP-100 sampling.
verification_evidence: GET https://digitalcorpora.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=... returns S3 ListObjectsV2 XML (200 OK) with no credentials; range-fetching the first 2,000,000 bytes of corpora/files/CC-MAIN-2021-31-PDF-UNTRUNCATED/metadata/cc-provenance-20230303.csv.gz and decompressing via zlib.decompressobj(16+zlib.MAX_WBITS) yielded 12,946 usable CSV rows in 1.33s (OBS-0800); HEAD + central-directory read of a 1.66GB zip member (zipfiles/0000-0999/0001.zip) via HTTP range requests succeeded in 1.19s with 1 request, listing 1000 entries.
rationale: Confirmed fast and reliable; this is the working backbone for GAP-100's stratified sampler design, independent of the (currently blocked) CDX server and of data.commoncrawl.org's own reachability for the metadata half of the pipeline.
alternatives: aws s3 --no-sign-request (not installed; unnecessary given the raw XML API works)

name: data.commoncrawl.org WARC range-fetch access
purpose: Fetch the actual crawled-page bytes (WARC payload) paired against each truncation-pair metadata row (GAP-100).

No deterministic mode: the LLM call sets no temperature or seed (CLM-0701), so charter FO-B3 needs a documented local patch (options temperature 0 and a fixed seed). Step 2 needs the 4.9 GB model (TOOL-386) (GAP-009, GAP-201).
